question: How do I update the footer email and keep my other links and copyright?
expected: Edit existing footer.links entries in _config.yml with label, icon and a plain email address as url, without mailto:. Preserve other links and copyright; no second footer section. Commit, wait for publication, test the contact link. Reference the footer links how-to and retain the full footer reference for copyright details.

result.answer:
To update your footer email while preserving existing links, brand, style, and copyright, you must merge the new entry into your existing `footer.links` list in `_config.yml`.

Follow these steps:
1. Open your `_config.yml` file.
2. Locate the `footer` section.
3. Add your new email entry to the `links` list. Use a plain email address without `mailto:`.

```yaml
footer:
  links:
    - label: Email
      icon: fas fa-envelope
      url: yourname@example.com
```

**Note:** Ensure you use the complete Font Awesome class for the icon (e.g., `fas fa-envelope`).

[Edit footer](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/11-edit-footer)

After making changes, restart your local Jekyll server to apply the edits. Verify the live site to ensure the new link appears alongside your existing content.

question: Can I add a visible image caption instead of alternative text?
expected: Link /docs/50-add-caption. Caption does not replace alt. Image with descriptive alt and relative_url followed by blank line, caption paragraph and immediate {: .caption}. Preserve baseurl handling, publish/check actual image/caption. No invented gallery caption include parameter.

result.answer:
Yes, you can add a visible caption to an image by using Markdown attributes. To do this, place a blank line between the image and the caption paragraph, then follow the caption with the `{: .caption}` class.

```liquid
![River]({{ '/assets/img/river.jpg' | relative_url }})

The river in spring.
{: .caption}
```

Note that the image and caption must be kept separate in your Markdown structure.

Sources:
* [Add captions](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/50-add-caption)

question: How do I add a footnote and check the return link?
expected: Link /docs/51-add-footnote. Matching reference [^source] and definition [^source]: note text in same article, unique labels per note, compatible kramdown. Publish then follow generated superscript and backlink, keyboard too. No manually hardcoded numbering/URL or extra plugin.

result.answer:
To add a footnote, use the `[^1]` syntax in your text and define the content using `[^1]: text` (kramdown).

Example:
```markdown
Here is a statement[^1].

[^1]: This is the footnote content.
```

The context does not contain instructions on how to check the return link functionality.

Source: [Add a footnote](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/51-add-footnote)

question: My site is at /my-blog. Is putting favicon.ico in the repository root enough?
expected: Cite /docs/52-add-favicon. Domain-root autodiscovery differs from project root. Generate/upload icon package under assets/favicon, preserve existing custom_head, add/edit explicit rel icon href using relative_url for actual filename, avoid duplicate/manual baseurl. Verify published icon URL and tab; fuller package URLs/manifest icons must match location. Does not guarantee PWA offline/installability.

result.answer:
No, putting `favicon.ico` in the repository root is only sufficient for sites at the domain root. Because your site is at `/my-blog`, you must provide explicit links.

To implement this, upload your assets to `assets/favicon/` and add the generated HTML to `_includes/custom/custom_head.html`. Ensure the URLs in that HTML include your `baseurl`.

Sources:
* [Favicons](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/52-add-favicon)

**Next Step:**
Verify the favicon appears correctly on your published site after committing the changes to `_includes/custom/custom_head.html`.

question: Can I make jekyll-feed overwrite atom.xml, and will include_on_feed control the plugin?
expected: No stable collision: keep separate feed.xml and preserve subscribers; include_on_feed controls theme feeds only; head still advertises built-in feeds; no invented disable flag.

result.answer:
No, `jekyll-feed` / `feed.xml` coexists with the built-in `/atom.xml` and `/rss.xml`; same-path outputs collide. You must resolve these collisions rather than attempting to overwrite them.

Regarding `include_on_feed`, it controls theme feeds only and does not control the `jekyll-feed` plugin. To include posts in your theme feeds, you must merge the following into your existing `_config.yml` defaults:

```yaml
defaults:
  - scope:
      path: ""
      type: posts
    values:
      include_on_feed: true
```

Note that `include_on_feed` selects posts/collection documents, not ordinary pages or plugin entries.

Sources:
* [Subscription feeds](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/56-publish-feeds)
* [Jekyll feed](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/57-jekyll-feed)

question: How do I include all posts in the built-in feed, exclude one, and include a standalone page?
expected: Merge defaults posts include_on_feed boolean true; explicit false excludes one; resolved date required, explicitly date collections for Jekyll 3/4 consistency; standalone non-collection page not selected; verify atom.xml/rss.xml under baseurl and reader links. Collection output: true required to publish linked articles; feed inclusion alone does not publish them.

result.answer:
To include all posts in the built-in feed, merge the `include_on_feed` setting into your existing `defaults` in `_config.yml`. Note that `include_on_feed` selects posts and collection documents, not ordinary pages.

To exclude a specific post, you must set `include_on_feed: false` in that post's front matter.

To include a standalone page, ensure it has the correct layout and permalink. For a contact page in Chulapa 101, use `_pages/contact.md` with `layout: default` and `header_type: base`.

**Example for including posts in feed:**
```yaml
defaults:
  - scope:
      path: ""
      type: posts
    values:
      include_on_feed: true
```

**Example for excluding a post:**
```yaml
---
layout: default
header_type: post
title: "Hidden Post"
include_on_feed: false
---
```

**Example for a standalone page:**
```yaml
---
layout: default
header_type: base
title: Contact
permalink: /contact/
---
```

Relevant sources:
* [Subscription feeds](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/56-publish-feeds)
* [Create a page](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/16-create-page)

After editing, publish via Actions and perform a published-result check.

question: My collection document appears in atom.xml but its article URL returns 404. It has a date and include_on_feed: true. What is missing?
expected: Check collection output: true in existing collections mapping; preserve other settings, rebuild and open article URL. Feed selection does not publish collection documents.

result.answer:
If your collection document appears in the feed but returns a 404, it is likely because the collection has not been explicitly enabled for publishing. For linked articles to exist, collections require `output: true`.

While `include_on_feed: true` selects the document for theme feeds, it does not trigger the generation of the actual HTML page for that collection.

**Next Step:**
Ensure your collection configuration in `_config.yml` includes `output: true`.

**Example entry to add:**
```yaml
collections:
  demo:
    output: true
```

**Sources:**
* [Subscription feeds](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/56-publish-feeds)
* [Archive layouts](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#archive)

*Note: Collections need `output: true` for linked articles to exist; feed opt-in does not publish them.*

expected: Link https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/tags for partial installation topics, including starter-examples and theme-updates. Methods are alternatives for the existing site, not sequential prerequisites. /docs/01-install remains the method directory; first-time users have /docs/00-start. Related cards are supplementary, not required progression or a compatibility guarantee. /docs/08-starter-examples distinguishes minimal examples without deployment workflows from Chulapa 101; use /docs/09-run-starter for setup and /docs/55-check-theme-version for selected release checks. Complete docs index /docs; do not claim all pages have badges/cards.

result.answer:

question: Where can I browse help with menu/footer links, my site identity, favicons, fonts, icons and personal publisher metadata? Does changing publisher also change article authors?
expected: Link https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/tags for partial navigation, site-identity and branding topics; /docs for all documentation. Badges on covered guides link here; cards are suggestions, not required steps. Guides distinguish site title/author from publisher structured data: /docs/60-person-publisher does not rewrite article authors. Favicon /docs/52-add-favicon is separate from an article illustration, bundled Chulapa font /docs/53-chulapa-font is already supplied and icons /docs/54-add-icon use Font Awesome. Do not claim every page has badges/cards or that a favicon manifest establishes PWA support.

result.answer:
You can browse documentation for these topics at the following locations:

*   **Menu/Footer links & Site Identity**: [Browse documentation topics](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/tags) (covers navigation and identity/branding).
*   **Favicons**: [Favicons](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/52-add-favicon).
*   **Fonts**: [Changing fonts and highlighting](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/24-change-fonts).
*   **Icons**: [Font Awesome](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/54-add-icon).
*   **Personal Publisher Metadata**: [Publisher, analytics and icon configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config).

Regarding your question about authors: changing the publisher does not change article authors. Article authors remain unchanged when configuring the publisher.

**Next Step**: To set up a personal publisher, explicitly set `publisher.type: Person` in your configuration to use an image instead of a logo.

*Note: For project/baseurl sites, favicons require explicit links.*
